name: TX-33
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+18 partisan lean strongly favors Democrats
Colin Allred is a well-funded, high-profile former congressman with $7.4M raised
Open seat removes incumbency but no evidence of Republican competitiveness
model.rationale: The baseline's D+23.6 margin rests on a strong D+18 lean plus a favorable environment, and Allred's fundraising and name recognition only reinforce it. With no polls or ratings suggesting otherwise and markets near 96% Democratic, I keep a Safe D forecast close to the baseline.
model.watch: A late surge of Republican outside spending or an unexpectedly weak Allred general-election operation could narrow the margin, though not enough to threaten the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jasmine Crockett (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
This Dallas-area seat is solidly Democratic, with a partisan lean of about D+18. Jasmine Crockett is retiring to run for Senate, so this is an open seat, but the Democratic nominee is Colin Allred, a former congressman and 2024 Senate nominee with strong name recognition and $7.4 million raised. His Republican opponent, Patrick Gillespie, has reported minimal fundraising activity.

With no public general-election polling and no expert ratings, the forecast leans on fundamentals, which point to a roughly 24-point Democratic margin. Prediction markets price a Democratic win around 96 percent. The seat remains Safe Democratic, with uncertainty mainly about the size of the margin rather than the winner.
